socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announced a new 2026 ARC-AGI-2 Kaggle high of 88.06% by Tufa Labs and said a $150,000 bonus would be split among teams scoring above 85%.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A public-board threshold announcement and major standings lead; the post does not establish a final private score.

socialPosts.author: crysis44k
socialPosts.summary: In Japanese, fshindo said they had finally reached the medal range in ARC-AGI-2 and were pleased after spending substantial effort on it. This is the author’s claim; no primary profile link connecting @crysis44k to a specific Kaggle team has been verified. A similar board name and the attached image do not establish that connection.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A fresh ARC-2 competitor reaction for the evening desk. Verify the account-to-team connection and evening board before combining it with team 17019785 or reporting a provisional medal-band position as fact.

socialPosts.author: cunkpyber
socialPosts.summary: PunkCyber tells the ARC Daily Digest that 復活の混テキスト is their team. The exact Japanese name matches entries on the current ARC-3 and ARC-2 boards; these have separate competition team IDs.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A competitor checked in with the paper and supplied a direct team identification. It supports a friendly shout-out; the reply does not identify their individual Kaggle handle or establish who produced a submission.

socialPosts.author: masspeakss
socialPosts.summary: masspeaks reacted in Japanese to Tufa Labs exceeding 85% on ARC-AGI-2, calling the result impressive. The public board independently shows Tufa Labs at 88.06% in the afternoon snapshot.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Respectful reaction from a current ARC-AGI-2 mover to the leader.

socialPosts.author: masspeakss
socialPosts.summary: In a Japanese post, masspeaks said careful preparation had paid off and expected a high gold-band cutoff. This is the contestant’s reaction; the post alone does not establish the exact score or method.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Context from the ARC-AGI-2 public-board mover; compare any score or rank with the board brief.

socialPosts.author: tufalabs
socialPosts.summary: In a reply to Mike Knoop’s ARC-AGI-2 bonus-threshold post, Tufa Labs said it had not set out to solve ARC-AGI-2, started by accident, and plans to share more after the deadline. This is the team’s account, not an independently established history.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: First-person context from the ARC-AGI-2 public-board leader; no method or final result is disclosed.

socialPosts.author: JFPuget
socialPosts.summary: Puget asked ARC Prize whether the 85% bonus threshold refers to the public or private leaderboard; no organizer answer was visible in the checked thread.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Flags a reporting question; avoid presenting the public score as the final prize result.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Knoop said ARC-AGI-2 remains much harder than ARC-AGI-1 and that eventual open solutions will be useful to study, while quoting his earlier reaction to Tufa Labs crossing the public Kaggle bonus threshold.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Organizer context about the contest; his forward-looking statement is not a released solution or final award.

socialPosts.author: mikeknoop
socialPosts.summary: Knoop said the 85% Grand Prize bonus threshold had been reached on Kaggle and called 2026 the final ARC-AGI-2 Kaggle year.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Provides organizer context for the Tufa Labs result; his expectation about future open artifacts is not yet a release.

socialPosts.author: fchollet
socialPosts.summary: Chollet reacted to ARC Prize’s Tufa Labs ARC-2 announcement by saying Kaggle scores are getting very good.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A founder reaction adds a measured voice to the organizer’s score announcement.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize announced Stephen Wolfram as a keynote speaker for its 2026 Research Summit.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: A current event-program lead for the meeting digest.

socialPosts.author: JFPuget
socialPosts.summary: Jean-François Puget warns that setting temperature to zero does not guarantee fully deterministic LLM inference. The post quotes a claim that temperature zero always produces the same answer. In a later reply he says the hiring wording should not be taken too seriously and was intended to draw attention to the topic.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: Older catch-up lead for reporting on reproducibility and run-to-run variation. This is Puget’s general inference comment, not a measurement explaining any ARC leaderboard result. Preserve the clarification when using the hiring line.

socialPosts.author: arcprize
socialPosts.summary: ARC Prize published verified Grok 4.7 scores: 1.8% on ARC-AGI-3 with its standard harness, 10.0% with a provider adapter, and 61.4% on ARC-AGI-2.
socialPosts.whyItMatters: The harness distinction matters when comparing model scores; the post reports organizer verification.

socialPosts.author: arcprize

dispatches.headline: Afternoon edition: ARC Raiders reaches 62.08 as the ARC-2 gold line rises

sections.heading: Raiders strengthens its top-ten place
sections.text: ARC Raiders has lifted its ARC-AGI-2 score from 60.00 to 62.08 in a recorded overnight improvement, retaining eighth. Its checked roster lists dzjiann, keithtyser, mitubant and ngyzly. Tyser, dzjiann and mitubant are also listed with ARC Slayers, now seventh on ARC-AGI-3. Raiders is a top-ten contender in its own contest; Tufa Labs still leads ARC-AGI-2.

sections.heading: The leaders hold while gold gets more expensive
sections.text: Tufa Labs remains at 88.06, followed by rabbithole at 80.56, Yi-Chia Chen at 77.22 and nvbanana at 77.08. The score for the last of 15 public gold places has risen to 44.44, up 2.63 in the fresh past-day comparison. Sam-wiz is the first team outside that band, sixteenth at 41.81. Public gold-band membership remains provisional until the private-board finish.

sections.heading: Schweighofer is inside gold; Odd Dice reaches the low thirties
sections.text: Kajetan Schweighofer is twelfth at 47.92 after an 11.25-point gain in the past-day comparison. nvnn is fourteenth at 45.00. Below gold, Odd Dice has reached 31st at 36.53; the previous-close comparison shows it up from 113th with a 4.03-point gain. The much larger early Wire climbs remain worth following too: mrkmakr is now thirtieth and Burton Lancaster 35th.

sections.heading: Tufa promises its account after the deadline
sections.text: In its October 10 reply to Mike Knoop, Tufa Labs said ARC-AGI-2 was the one ARC challenge it had not set out to solve, described its start as accidental and promised more information after the deadline. That is the team’s own account, with the method still unrevealed. It gives readers a specific post-competition story to look forward to.

sections.heading: The Research Summit is eleven days away
sections.text: ARC Prize’s Research Summit is scheduled for October 23 in Boston, hosted by the Foundation in collaboration with MIT. Its focus is the meeting point of neural networks, program synthesis and formal reasoning—a timely setting for the rulebook and harness questions circulating around ARC-AGI-3.
